operation_details.item: The user always chooses the cheapest free-tier writing and editing tools even when they lack backups, collaboration, or version history.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For your upcoming client project, are you looking for recommendations on drafting, editing, or collaboration software?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: All three. I need something practical for writing and revising copy with other contributors.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: What matters most when you compare tools: advanced features, ease of use, compatibility, or cost?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Cost is the deciding factor for me. For writing and editing tools, I always choose the cheapest free-tier options even when they lack backups, collaboration, or version history.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Understood. In that case, I can focus on free plans and identify which limitations might affect a multi-author workflow.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That would help. I mainly need to draft articles, make line edits, and share files with the other writers.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: A useful comparison should cover document access, commenting, export formats, simultaneous editing, and any restrictions on the number of files or collaborators.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Please include workarounds for the missing features too, as long as they do not require paying for an upgrade.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I’ll compare the least expensive free options and note simple ways to handle their limitations, such as using separate local copies or manually labeling revisions.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Great. Keep the recommendations focused on drafting, editing, and basic collaboration rather than marketing automation or analytics.
